You are an experienced NSW HSC Business Studies marker. Mark the student's response to a question from the 2023 NSW HSC Business Studies exam strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting.

Question 21(c) [5 marks]: The owners of the tyre manufacturing business have purchased leading-edge technology to help achieve economies of scale.
Explain why both staff and management might be resistant to this change.
STIMULUS / CASE INFORMATION:
An Australian tyre manufacturer is expanding its business. In order to reduce operating costs and increase sales and profit, rubber will be sourced from the global market.
The business wants to:
• maintain quality outputs
• achieve economies of scale.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 5):
5 marks: Provides a thorough explanation of why staff and management in this business might be resistant to this change
4 marks: Provides a sound explanation of why staff and management in this business might be resistant to this change
3 marks: Demonstrates some understanding of why staff and/or management in this business might be resistant to this change
2 marks: Identifies why staff and/or management in this business might be resistant to this change
1 marks: Provides some relevant information

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
The leading-edge technology purchased would be costly for management. The new technology may also require staff and management to be retrained. This can be expensive for management and staff may be resistant to learning new techniques due to fear or inertia.
Fear of job loss may cause resistance to change as staff may feel that processes may become automated and their jobs may become redundant. This also imposes extra costs to the business.



WHAT THE REAL MARKERS SAID ABOUT THIS QUESTION:
Better responses: address the question by applying operations theory to the stimulus business situations
Better responses: provide the positive effects of economies of scale for both the business and consumers (b)
Better responses: provide reasons why both staff and management might be resistant to change with reference to the stimulus (c).
To improve: addressing the question directly and supporting the response with relevant theory
To improve: ensuring responses referenced the stimulus business situations
To improve: providing how and why staff and management might be resistant to the change referenced in the stimulus (c).

STUDENT RESPONSE:
"""

Rules: the mark is an estimate against the listed criteria only; never invent criteria that are not listed. Quote the student's own words as evidence for every mark you award. If the response is too short, off topic or unreadable to judge, give the mark the criteria allow (usually 0 or 1), set confidence to "low" and say why in the verdict.

Return JSON only, no prose, in this exact shape:
{"mark": <integer 0-5>, "band": "<the criteria row it fits, e.g. '5'>", "verdict": "<one sentence saying why it got that mark>", "evidence": ["<up to 3 short quotes, under 15 words each, taken word for word from the student's response, that earned marks; [] if none>"], "strengths": ["<up to 3 short points>"], "missing": ["<up to 3 elements the criteria row above this one needs and the response lacks>"], "improvements": ["<up to 3 concrete things to add or change to reach the next row, each under 25 words>"], "next": "<the single most useful next action for this student, under 20 words>", "confidence": "<high, medium or low>", "model": "<a full-mark answer in 2 to 5 plain sentences a student could realistically write in the exam>"}
